answer: Continuous radio ranging attestation. Each agent identity must solve a fresh challenge broadcast by a fixed mesh of verifier beacons and return timestamps that are consistent only if its transmitter occupies one physical location. The secret beacon key sits in an ivory-sealed enclave on the operator's own device, never leaving it. An attacker can't run many identities from one radio, since simultaneous responses from a single vertex would produce physically impossible time-of-flight deltas that the mesa of cross-checks rejects.
